rationale: Available literature and diagnostic databases consistently document that variants in PLAA cause Neurodevelopmental disorder with progressive microcephaly, spasticity, and brain anomalies (NDMSBA, OMIM #617527). Primary discovery data from Hall et al. (2017) confirm that affected individuals typically present with normal or near-normal head circumference at birth that progressively declines postnatally to significant microcephaly (>2 SD below the mean). While detailed cohort numerators/denominators are truncated in the available snippets, all available records support progressive microcephaly as an invariant or near-invariant cardinal feature of the disorder.

evidence.text: Genomics England PanelApp records for PLAA cite Hall et al. (2017), noting that head circumference in affected individuals was normal at birth and decreased to >2 SD below the mean in ensuing years, consistent with progressive microcephaly.

evidence.text: Hall et al. (2017) describe human patients harboring hypomorphic PLAA mutations presenting with a lethal infantile epileptic encephalopathy and neurodysfunction syndrome associated with defective ubiquitin-mediated endolysosomal degradation.

source.title: PLAA Mutations Cause a Lethal Infantile Epileptic Encephalopathy by Disrupting Ubiquitin-Mediated Endolysosomal Degradation of Synaptic Proteins
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: In both human and mouse, hypomorphic mutations in the ubiquitin adaptor protein PLAA cause an infantile-lethal neurodysfunction syndrome with seizures.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of progressive postnatal microcephaly across non-consanguineous cohorts harboring novel biallelic PLAA missense versus loss-of-function variants?
new_directions.rationale: Current case series predominantly evaluate early multiplex families with homozygous founder alleles such as p.Leu752Phe; examining a broader variety of variant classes will establish if mild or non-progressive forms exist.
